_how_to_use: PASTE ONLY THE `prompt` FIELD INTO THE IMAGE MODEL. Nothing else in this file is for the model. Pasting the whole file produced a collage of several captioned slides, because `renditions_wanted` lists two sizes, `framing.aspect_ratios` lists two ratios, and headline_in_app / caption_in_app are text - the model read all of that as a brief to draw multiple frames with words on them. Those fields are for the render pipeline and for whoever writes the app copy.
_source_image_note: Save the image you keep in this folder named `03_welcome_3_library_stays_yours` with whatever extension the model gave you - .jpg, .png, .jpeg and .webp are all accepted. Only the NAME has to match this file; the extension does not. lessons/scripts/tutor_images.py then renders it to renders/03_welcome_3_library_stays_yours/ as slide_1080x1920 (9:16 phone slide) and card_1080x1350 (4:5). Renditions are always written as PNG regardless of the source format.
audience: the learner setting up their own account
caption_in_app: Every lesson you attend is saved to rewatch any time - even between subscriptions.
intent: what you have built is yours to keep - a shelf of finished work and a lesson you can return to, seen over the shoulder
prompt: A single photograph, one continuous scene, filling the whole frame. Shot from behind and slightly to one side, over the shoulder of an Indian South African boy of about 17 seated at a small desk in their own bedroom on a bright Saturday morning. We see the back of their head and shoulders, the desk, and the wall in front of them: a shelf holding a row of eight or ten used exercise books standing on their spines, a full year of work. On the desk an older exercise book lies open at pages already filled with handwriting, and a tablet sits in a small black folding stand pushed to the side, screen angled away from camera so nothing on it is readable. Morning light from a window to the left. Upright posture, unhurried. The room is ordinary and lived-in - a school shirt on a hook, a wardrobe edge in frame.
negative_prompt: any text, letters, numbers, words, signage, logos, watermarks, user-interface elements, phone screens showing apps, charts or graphs, cartoon, illustration, 3d render, cgi, airbrushed skin, plastic sheen, cinematic colour grade, film still look, motion blur, lens flare, extra fingers, malformed hands, distorted faces, stock-photo smiles, American classrooms, generic 'African' styling, collage, multiple panels, split screen, side-by-side frames, contact sheet, grid of images, storyboard, several phone mockups, device frames, app screenshots, before-and-after, picture-in-picture, borders, margins, framed print, lying down, lying on a bed, slouching, sprawled, in pyjamas, under a duvet, phone in bed, night-time bedroom, idle scrolling, device floating in mid-air, phone standing on nothing, tablet balanced impossibly upright, no visible support, object hovering

_pipeline_only._note: NOT model input - read by the render script and the app.

framing.composition: subject in the lower two thirds, calm uncluttered space in the upper third where the slide's headline and caption sit - the image must never compete with the copy
framing.safe_area: keep the top 28% and bottom 18% visually quiet: the headline sits above, the button below

_revision_note: Rewritten 2026-07-30 (owner): the first version had the learner lying on a bed late at night with an earphone in. On a study product that reads as lounging and teaches the wrong habit on the third slide a student ever sees. Same promise - the lesson is yours to return to - shown as upright daytime revision instead. Follow-up: 'No bed, nobody lying down, nothing about night-time' was removed from the POSITIVE prompt. Image models handle negation badly, and naming a bed is a reliable way to get one; exclusions belong in negative_prompt, where these already are.
_support_note: The device rests on something NAMED. 'Propped-up' describes the result, not the support, so the model rendered a phone standing upright on nothing (owner, 2026-07-30). A stack of exercise books or a cheap folding stand is both plausible in a South African home and something the model can actually draw in contact with the device.
_distinct_from_siblings: Rewritten 2026-07-30 (owner): the first render of this slide was indistinguishable from slide 01 - same boy, same white t-shirt, same dining table, same window. My prompts differed only in LIGHTING and in an abstraction ('going back over an earlier lesson'), and a model cannot render 'earlier'. Now it differs on three photographable axes: room (bedroom desk, not the dining table), camera (over the shoulder from behind, not front three-quarter), and time (Saturday morning). The promise is made physical as a shelf of used exercise books, which can be photographed - accumulation reads as ownership.
_casting_note: Cast as an Indian South African boy of about 17 (owner, 2026-07-30). The prompts said only 'a South African teenager'/'parent', so the model defaulted and EVERY slide came back Black and male. The onboarding carousel is the first thing anyone sees on a national platform - a learner should be able to find themselves in it. students/01 and students/04 keep their approved casting; majority representation is right, it just cannot be the only representation.
